clue.text: Fond of acting round the West End

indicators.note: to go round something is to enclose it, so one piece wraps about the other

parts.note: acting is doing, as in 'what are you doing?'

indicators.note: on a page west is the left, so the western end of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the left-hand letter of this little word

explanation.surface: Someone besotted with the stage and the London theatre district.
explanation.walkthrough: The West End is London's theatreland, which suits 'acting' perfectly, but here it means the left-hand end of 'the'. DOTING has T inside DOING.
explanation.definitionFit: Doting means excessively loving, so it is a synonym for being very fond.

clue.text: It's the first thing with beginners

definitions.text: It's the first thing with beginners

parts.note: surface reading: the opening lesson for novices
setter's reading: the stage call 'beginners, please' summons actors who appear first, just as the orchestra starts the opening music

explanation.walkthrough: In theatre 'beginners' are the cast on stage at curtain-up; the opening piece of music comes first with them.
explanation.definitionFit: An overture is the instrumental introduction to an opera or show, the very first thing heard at the start.

clue.text: Nitre disposed of round river, away from the coast

indicators.note: to go round something is to surround it, so one piece encloses the other
things disposed are arranged or set out afresh, so the letters are laid out anew

parts.note: rio is the Spanish and Portuguese word for river
the five letters of this word rearranged

explanation.surface: A chemist gets rid of saltpetre near a river, some way inland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disposed of' looks like throwing away, but here it means arranged. RIO goes inside INTE_R.
explanation.definitionFit: The interior of a country is the inland region, the part away from the coast.

clue.text: One dancer, for example, when mixing a drink

definitions.note: the answer is a mixer, used when mixing a drink

parts.note: Ginger Rogers, Fred Astaire's partner, is one famous dancer
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A dancer hard at work at a cocktail bar.
explanation.walkthrough: Ginger Rogers, Fred Astaire's partner, is the dancer. The definition is loose: ginger ale is a mixer, the thing you use when mixing drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Ginger ale is a sweet fizzy soft drink commonly added to spirits such as whisky, which makes it a mixer.

clue.text: Stars in festival team given points

parts.note: a gala is a festive occasion
a cricket or football team has eleven players, written in Roman numerals
two compass points, east and south

explanation.surface: A sports side at a festival is awarded points, as if in a competition.
explanation.walkthrough: XI for a team is the Roman eleven of a cricket or football side.
explanation.definitionFit: Galaxies are vast systems containing billions of stars, so the plural word stands for them.

clue.text: Inexperienced musician takes spirits and gets the bird

parts.note: a green recruit is a novice
Sir Henry Wood, the conductor who founded the Proms
pecker is British slang for spirits or courage, as in 'keep your pecker up'

explanation.surface: A novice performer drinks spirits and is booed off stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets the bird' is an idiom for being jeered; here it just ends with the definition. Henry Wood founded the London Proms concerts.
explanation.definitionFit: The green woodpecker is a common British bird with green plumage and a laughing call, so it is an example of a bird.

clue.text: Shakespearean ice-cream vendor

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the merchant in The Merchant of Venice
second meaning: the stock Italian ice-cream seller of the old music-hall song

explanation.walkthrough: The old song 'O Antonio' made the name the stereotype of the Italian ice-cream man in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonio is a character in several Shakespeare plays and the name of the comic ice-cream seller in a popular British song.

clue.text: International dealer advertises as a carrier

parts.note: someone advertising themselves announces 'I'm ...'
a porter carries luggage

explanation.surface: An overseas trader promotes himself as a haulage firm.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is the declaration 'I'm porter', which is how a carrier advertises himself.
explanation.definitionFit: An importer brings in goods from abroad to sell, so it is a dealer in international trade.

clue.text: Careless hit and run

parts.note: to slap is to hit
to dash is to run

explanation.surface: A careless hit-and-run driver.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapdash describes work done hastily and without care, so it is a synonym for careless.

clue.text: A few words from the judge

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a grammatical unit of several words
second meaning: the punishment a judge passes on a convicted person

explanation.surface: A judge says a few words in court.
explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one phrase about a judge speaking, but the grammar term and the court punishment are two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentence is both a string of words in grammar and the penalty pronounced by a court after conviction.

clue.text: More work for a university First with excellent recall

parts.note: standard abbreviation for university
first place is the top

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the letters are taken back the other way

parts.note: A1 means excellent, with the 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: Extra study needed at university to get a first-class degree with an excellent memory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More' is not 'extra' but Sir Thomas More, whose most famous book is Utopia. A1 is British slang for first-rate, with the 1 read as a letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Thomas More wrote Utopia in 1516, so the book title is literally a work by More.

clue.text: Way to encourage fish

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
to urge on is to encourage

explanation.surface: A method for coaxing fish along.
explanation.definitionFit: The sturgeon is a large fish, famous as the source of caviar, so it is an example of fish.

clue.text: Popular network girl

parts.note: something popular is in fashion
a grid is a network, as of electricity cables or streets

explanation.surface: A girl who is a favourite on a television network.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingrid is a woman's first name, and crosswords treat any such name as an example of a girl.

clue.text: Musical work "The Plaintiff in Chancery and the Priestess"

parts.note: in old Chancery pleadings the petitioner styled himself 'your orator'
Io was a priestess of Hera in Greek myth

explanation.surface: It looks like the title of a piece, a courtroom drama with a priestess in it.
explanation.walkthrough: Chancery was an English court of equity, where a complainant was formally called the orator. Io was the priestess loved by Zeus and turned into a heifer.
explanation.definitionFit: An oratorio is a large-scale musical composition on a sacred theme, like Handel's Messiah, so it is a musical work.

clue.text: People thought to have leanings towards 10

parts.note: a thought is an idea
a ship that leans to one side lists, so leanings are lists
padding that rounds off the picture: such people do lean towards 10 across, the perfect imaginary state

explanation.surface: Some people are suspected of hankering after an ideal society.
explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a whole-clue description, and in a sense it is, but the words also split: 'thought' and 'leanings' build the answer. 10 across is UTOPIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Idealists are persons who pursue lofty, often impractical principles, so the plural noun stands for people of that kind.

clue.text: For, say, a buck, it's expensive

indicators.note: to say a word is to speak it, so we want its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: a buck is a male deer

explanation.surface: Something that costs a buck, a dollar, is called pricey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buck' looks like a dollar, which fits 'expensive', but it is the male animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Dear is an established British word for costly or high-priced, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Arbitrary mark involved in playing dice

indicators.note: dice in play are thrown and land jumbled, so these letters are reordered
something involved in another is wrapped up inside it

parts.note: the four letters of this word rearranged
a spot is a mark or stain

explanation.surface: A random blemish turns up in a game of dice.
explanation.walkthrough: SPOT goes inside DE_IC.
explanation.definitionFit: A despotic ruler wields absolute power on a whim, so the adjective means arbitrary in the sense of unrestrained.

clue.text: The end of him, we hear, can be easily managed

indicators.note: what we hear is a spoken sound, so one word is replaced by another sounding the same

parts.note: the word sung at the close of a hymn
able means one can do something

explanation.surface: A man dies; the rest are tractable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Him' is heard as 'hymn', and the word sung at the close of every hymn is the wordplay's first part.
explanation.definitionFit: Amenable means compliant and responsive to persuasion, so a person who is amenable is easily managed.

clue.text: Chief supporter

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a curved structure that holds up a bridge or roof

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a leading fan, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Arch is an adjective for principal or foremost, and also a noun for a curved structure bearing weight above an opening.

clue.text: Book about races an artist draws

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds the others

parts.note: the Acts of the Apostles, a book of the New Testament
the TT, Tourist Trophy, motorcycle races on the Isle of Man
a Royal Academician

explanation.surface: A book on motor racing by a painter who sketches.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an illustrated book, but 'draws' is the definition, in the sense of pulling in a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw a crowd is to attract it, so draws in the sense of pulls towards is a synonym.

clue.text: Indian accepts a judge, having no worries

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: the Cree are a Native American people
taken as written
a referee judges a game

explanation.surface: A Native American takes on a judge and is untroubled.
explanation.walkthrough: A REF goes inside C_REE.
explanation.definitionFit: Carefree means free from anxiety or responsibility, so it describes someone without worries.

clue.text: Lazy type gets very tired

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an idle, feckless person
second meaning: as two words, utterly exhausted

explanation.surface: An idler wears himself out, ironically.
explanation.walkthrough: The noun is one word; the second meaning splits it into two, as in 'I'm dead beat'.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadbeat is an idle loafer, and 'dead beat' is an informal phrase for completely exhausted.

clue.text: "He's made to dwell in a — cell" (Gilbert)

parts.words: He's made to dwell in a — cell
parts.note: surface reading: a line of verse with a word missing
setter's reading: fill the gap from W. S. Gilbert's song in The Mikado about fitting the punishment to the crime

explanation.walkthrough: The line comes from 'A more humane Mikado': the offender is made to dwell in an underground prison cell.
explanation.definitionFit: A dungeon is an underground prison, and the quotation describes a cell of exactly that kind.

clue.text: Longing to fix half of 12

parts.note: to fix something in place is to pin it

indicators.note: half of a word means only one of its two halves is kept

parts.note: the opening three letters of the six-letter answer to 12 across

explanation.surface: A wish to repair something half broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 12 refers to the answer INGRID; its first half is ING.
explanation.definitionFit: Pining is yearning or wasting away with desire, so it is a synonym for longing in the participle form.

clue.text: Extended oriental dangler gets broken

parts.note: E for East

indicators.note: something broken falls to pieces, and its pieces can be put back in another order

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An Eastern ornament hanging down is snapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Enlarged means made larger, so it is a synonym for extended in the past-participle form.

clue.text: Pill or vaccine authorised

parts.note: TAB is a vaccine against typhoid and paratyphoid A and B
let means allowed or permitted

explanation.surface: Is it a pill or an approved vaccine? A medical question.
explanation.walkthrough: TAB is the old name for the typhoid-paratyphoid vaccine given to soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A tablet is a compressed dose of medicine, which is exactly what a pill is.

clue.text: Lock taking bus, say, to play a game in Scotland

indicators.note: to say a word is to pronounce it, so its sound matters, not its spelling

parts.note: a buss is an old word for a kiss, and it sounds like this vehicle

parts.words: to play a game in Scotland
parts.note: curling, sliding stones on ice, is a sport especially associated with Scotland

explanation.surface: Someone catching a bus to a sporting fixture north of the border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lock' looks like a lock of hair only after the fact; the hyphenated answer is a single curl of hair pressed flat on the forehead or cheek.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiss-curl is a small flat curl of hair, and a lock is a tress, so this is an example of a lock.

clue.text: One who purifies soap, say

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a person who makes things clean
second meaning: a substance for washing, of which soap is an example

explanation.walkthrough: The same word covers the person doing the cleaning and the product used.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleanser is literally one that cleans or purifies, and soap is a typical washing product of that kind.

clue.text: Hospital worker put one in order

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a senior nurse in charge of a ward
second meaning: a nun, member of a religious order

explanation.surface: A nurse tidies a patient up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put one in order' sounds like tidying; the setter means a member of a religious order. 'Put' simply sets the two meanings side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: In British hospitals a sister is a senior ward nurse, and nuns in religious communities are also called sisters.
